name: FLIGHTDECK
shortDescription: Self-hosted deployment control plane for containers. Railway-style UI, your own hardware.
overview: A self-hosted deployment control plane for containers with Railway-style ergonomics on your own hardware. A small Rust agent on each host discovers labelled containers and streams their logs, metrics and status over WebSocket to a TypeScript control plane and a React UI, with gated restart and redeploy from the browser.

highlights.d: A Rust agent per server, against Docker or a rootless Podman socket, with automatic reconnect and live event fan-out.
Postgres LISTEN/NOTIFY fan-out, OIDC/JWT role-based access, and a read-only operator audit trail.
Durable log search via an optional Loki/Grafana/Prometheus stack, plus a notifications hub.

architecture.d: A TypeScript (Hono) service with two WebSocket endpoints, one for agents and one for browsers, keeping a bounded in-memory log tail per service and fanning events out to the UI.
One small static Rust binary per server that discovers containers labelled flightdeck.enable=true via the bollard Docker API and forwards logs, reconnecting automatically.
A versioned protocol package: zod schemas on the TypeScript side mirrored by serde structs in the Rust agent.

techDetails: CORE: Rust agent + TypeScript control plane + React 19 UI
HA: Postgres LISTEN/NOTIFY fan-out for multi-instance
AUTH: OIDC/JWT roles, constant-time agent tokens, local accounts (scrypt)
OBSERVABILITY: optional Loki / Grafana / Prometheus stack
TIERS: lite / medium / full via FD_PROFILE flags

name: ADW (AGENTIC DEV WORKFLOW)
shortDescription: A Python orchestrator for structured, crash-resumable AI agent runs.
overview: Agentic Developer Workflow: a Python orchestrator for running structured, repeatable AI agent workflows end to end. The run loop is split into per-kind step handlers with convergence signals and architectural gates, and it can suggest a workflow from the project's type. Tasks are idempotent, so a crashed or interrupted run resumes cleanly instead of starting over, and it wires git-local-issue as its issue sink and cargo-structure-diff as an architectural gate, keeping an agent's work both tracked and structurally honest.

highlights.d: A run loop split into per-kind step handlers, with convergence signals and architectural gates.
Idempotent tasks so an interrupted run resumes cleanly rather than latching a stale state.
Uses git-local-issue as an issue sink and cargo-structure-diff as an architectural deep gate.

techDetails: ORCHESTRATION: per-kind step handlers with convergence signals
RESUME: idempotent tasks survive crashes and restarts

name: SIMHARNESS
shortDescription: A deterministic, genre-agnostic harness for running and replaying coding agents reproducibly.
overview: A deterministic, genre-agnostic harness for running and replaying coding agents reproducibly, the eval substrate most agent setups lack. It is built around a discrete-action seam, so the same core drives spatial and non-spatial workers alike, with trace shrinking to reduce a failing run down to its minimal reproduction and porcelain action helpers for writing scenarios. Auto-generated API docs and a one-command quality gate keep it CI-friendly.

highlights.d: Run, replay and shrink agent traces reproducibly for reliable evaluation.
A discrete-action core that drives spatial and non-spatial workers alike.
Auto-generated API docs and a one-command quality gate.

techDetails: CORE: discrete-action seam, genre-agnostic
EVAL: trace shrinking and reproducible replay

name: PANEKIT
shortDescription: Headless terminal-UI test harness in Rust. Drive and assert real TUI state, no screen-scraping.
overview: A headless terminal-UI output and test harness in Rust, shipped as two crates: panedrive (the driver) and paneview (the state seam a terminal UI exposes). It lets an agent or a test press real keys and read real widget state instead of screen-scraping brittle text, so TUI behaviour can be asserted the way a web test asserts the DOM. It detects crashes and false passes, so a green run actually means the UI did what it claimed, and both crates are published to crates.io.

highlights.d: Press real keys and read real state from a TUI with no terminal attached.
CI-grade run results with crash and false-pass detection.
Shipped as two crates on crates.io (panedrive and paneview).

techDetails: CRATES: panedrive (driver) + paneview (state seam)
CI: crash and false-pass detection built in

name: CARGO-STRUCTURE-DIFF
shortDescription: A Rust CI gate that fails the build when a crate's module architecture drifts.
overview: A deterministic CI gate for Rust architecture, published on crates.io. It builds a stable structural IR of a crate, its modules, their relationships and public surface, then diffs that against a baseline and fails the build when the architecture drifts from what was agreed. It turns 'keep the structure clean' from a review-time opinion into an automated, reproducible check, so large refactors and AI-generated changes cannot quietly erode a codebase's shape.

highlights.d: Compares a crate's module structure against a baseline and flags drift.
A stable IR so the same code always yields the same verdict.
Available on crates.io, installable with cargo install.

techDetails: IR: stable structural representation of a crate
GATE: fails the build on architecture drift

name: GIT-LOCAL-ISSUE
shortDescription: Distributed, offline-first issue tracker that stores issues as native Git refs. No server.
overview: A distributed, offline-first issue tracker that stores issues natively in Git under refs/issues/*. No external database and no server: issues travel with the repo and sync over ordinary git. Each issue has a permanent UUIDv7 handle with human-friendly display numbers, and the whole tracker ships as a single Rust binary published to crates.io.

highlights.d: Issues live in refs/issues/*, versioned alongside the code they describe.
Create, edit and close issues with no network and no server.
Shipped on crates.io via cargo-dist.

techDetails: STORAGE: issues in refs/issues/* with UUIDv7 ids
SYNC: travels with the repo, no server required

name: LAZYDASH
shortDescription: Keyboard-driven terminal dashboard for GitHub Projects, backed by local Git issues.
overview: A keyboard-driven terminal dashboard for GitHub Projects, written in Go. It gives you multi-repo navigation, a roadmap view, and activity and calendar views derived from issue history, all without leaving the terminal. It can also back its issues with git-local-issue, so the board works fully offline and syncs through Git rather than depending on a hosted service.

highlights.d: Navigate GitHub Projects and multiple repos entirely from the keyboard.
Activity and calendar views derived from issue history.
Optional git-local-issue backend for offline work.

techDetails: VIEWS: activity and calendar from issue history
BACKEND: optional git-local-issue for offline work

name: COUNTER-INDEX
shortDescription: A high-throughput OP_NET data indexer: index, store and stream on-chain data.
overview: A high-throughput OP_NET data indexer: index, store and stream on-chain data. The read-side infrastructure for building on OP_NET, smart contracts on Bitcoin. It ingests blocks, normalizes events and exposes them to downstream services over a routing-aware, read-only surface, so applications can query OP_NET state without each running their own node.

highlights.d: Index, store and stream raw on-chain data to downstream consumers.
Read-only exposure and routing awareness for safe reads.
TypeScript services with Docker and type-aware tooling.

techDetails: PIPELINE: index, store and stream on-chain data
DEPLOY: containerized TypeScript services

name: MAXIBRIDGE
shortDescription: Cross-chain EVM to OP_NET bridge (smart contracts on Bitcoin). Audited by PeckShield.
overview: A cross-chain bridge between EVM chains and OP_NET (smart contracts on Bitcoin), with wrapped-asset contracts. Audited by PeckShield, with every finding resolved. The suite covers the wrapped ERC20 and OP20 mint and burn paths on both sides, hardened with pause guards and exercised by a shared test harness that runs the EVM and OP_NET flows together.

highlights.d: Reviewed by PeckShield; PVE findings addressed with pause guards and per-finding dispositions.
Wrapped ERC20 and OP20 assets bridged between EVM and OP_NET.
EVM and OP_NET test suites covering the bridge paths.

techDetails: AUDIT: PeckShield review, findings resolved
SUITES: EVM + OP_NET test coverage

name: DAEMON-WALLET
shortDescription: A Rust terminal EVM wallet that bridges to the browser. Daemon core plus Chrome front end.
overview: A Rust terminal EVM wallet (externally owned account) that bridges to the browser. It is a cargo workspace with a dedicated vault crate handling keys and signing, a long-running daemon core, and a Google Chrome front end that connects to it, so EVM transactions can be signed and sent from a terminal-first workflow while a familiar browser surface handles interaction. A proof of concept exploring where a wallet's trust boundary should sit.

highlights.d: A cargo workspace with a dedicated vault crate for key handling.
Connects the terminal daemon to a Google Chrome front end.
Signs and sends EVM transactions as an externally owned account.

techDetails: WORKSPACE: cargo workspace with a dedicated vault crate
BRIDGE: Rust daemon connects to a Chrome front end

name: SOLO STAKING
shortDescription: Liquid staking contracts for SOLO: stake SOLO, receive yield-bearing stSOLO.
overview: Foundry smart contracts for liquid staking on SOLO Chain. Users stake SOLO and receive stSOLO, a yield-bearing token that represents their staked position and accrues rewards through a tracked exchange rate, so their liquidity stays usable while it is staked. The suite ships with a full Foundry test suite, gas-focused test scripts, and deployment tooling.

highlights.d: Stake SOLO and receive stSOLO, a yield-bearing representation of the staked position.
Full Foundry test suite and deployment scripts.
Gas-mining test scripts and exchange-rate accounting.

techDetails: TOKEN: SOLO -> stSOLO liquid staking
TESTS: Foundry suite and deploy scripts

name: SOLO NFT MARKETPLACE
shortDescription: NFT marketplace supporting ERC721, ERC1155 and ERC6909, with safe-transfer patterns.
overview: An NFT marketplace contract suite for SOLO Chain that handles ERC721, ERC1155 and ERC6909 tokens in a single marketplace, a rare breadth that spans classic NFTs, multi-tokens, and the newer minimal multi-token standard. It applies safe-transfer patterns throughout to protect assets across the listing and settlement paths, and is covered by a Foundry test suite exercising the trading flows.

highlights.d: Supports ERC721, ERC1155 and ERC6909 in a single marketplace.
Uses safeTransferFrom and safeERC patterns for asset safety.
Foundry coverage across listing and settlement paths.

techDetails: STANDARDS: ERC721 / ERC1155 / ERC6909
SAFETY: safe-transfer patterns, Foundry-tested

name: MINEFUN
shortDescription: Smart contracts for the MineFun project on SOLO Chain, with security-first patterns.
overview: The on-chain contract suite for the MineFun project on SOLO Chain, written with security first. Reentrancy guards and the checks-effects-interactions pattern are applied throughout, with access restrictions on the sensitive entry points. It ships with a deployment pipeline and a TypeScript tooling layer, and a Foundry test suite covering the core flows.

highlights.d: Reentrancy guards and checks-effects-interactions across the contracts.
Deployment scripts with a TypeScript tooling layer.
Foundry test suite.

techDetails: SECURITY: reentrancy guards, checks-effects-interactions
TOOLING: Foundry plus a TypeScript deploy layer

name: SOLO GAS MINING
shortDescription: Gas / transaction mining system contracts for SOLO Chain.
overview: Foundry smart contracts implementing a gas, or transaction, mining system for SOLO Chain, which rewards on-chain activity as a mechanism to bootstrap network usage. The contracts are measured with gas-focused test scripts so the incentive maths holds up under real transaction costs, and they ship with deployment tooling and a Foundry test suite.

highlights.d: Rewards transaction activity through an on-chain mining mechanism.
Gas-focused test scripts and measurements.
Full Foundry suite and deploy scripts.

techDetails: MECHANISM: transaction / gas mining rewards
TESTS: gas-focused Foundry scripts

name: SOLO DEPIN BRIDGE
shortDescription: Cross-chain ERC721/1155 bridge to SOLO (as ERC6909) via MetaLayer.
overview: A cross-chain bridge that moves ERC721 and ERC1155 tokens from other chains onto SOLO Chain, representing them as ERC6909. It integrates with MetaLayer for cross-chain messaging and is source-domain-aware, so the origin chain is accounted for when minting the bridged representation, an important safety property for any bridge. It is covered by a Foundry test suite exercising the bridge paths.

highlights.d: Bridges ERC721 and ERC1155 assets to SOLO as ERC6909.
Integrated with MetaLayer, with source-domain awareness on bridging.
Foundry coverage of the bridge paths.

techDetails: BRIDGE: ERC721 / ERC1155 -> SOLO ERC6909 via MetaLayer
SAFETY: source-domain-aware, Foundry-tested
